title: Using commas, and marking what people say
canonical_examples_source: Language rules self-verified; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024-gps (KS2 GPS).

blocks.content: Commas tell the reader where to pause, and they keep a sentence clear. Let's learn two everyday jobs the comma does.
Use commas to separate three or more items in a list.

steps: The items are: apples, mangoes, bread.
Put a comma after each item except the last: 'I bought apples, mangoes and bread.'

blocks.prompt: Add the commas to this list: red green and blue
blocks.explain: Separate the list items with commas: red, green and blue.
blocks.rule: Use a comma to separate items in a list of three or more.

practiceItems.prompt: add commas: tea coffee and juice
add commas: dogs cats and birds
add commas: run jump and swim
add commas: rice peas and chicken

blocks.content: Use a comma to separate the name of the person you are speaking to: 'Come here, Sara.'

blocks.prompt: Add the comma: Thank you Mr Ali
blocks.explain: Put a comma before the name of the person you are speaking to: Thank you, Mr Ali.
blocks.rule: Use a comma to separate the name of the person you are speaking to from the rest of the sentence.

practiceItems.prompt: add a comma: Come here Sara
add a comma: Well done Maya

blocks.question: In the sentence Mum said Come inside, where should the quotation marks go?
options: Around the spoken words: Mum said, "Come inside."
Around the whole sentence including 'Mum said'
blocks.explain: Quotation marks go around the exact words a person says, not the words that tell us who is speaking. Only 'Come inside' is spoken, so the marks wrap just those words: Mum said, "Come inside."
blocks.rule: Quotation marks enclose only the exact spoken words.
blocks.principle: Punctuation shows the reader where speech begins and ends.
canonical_solution: Quotation marks wrap the spoken part

rubric.look_for: separates the spoken words from 'Mum said'
wraps only 'Come inside' in quotation marks
explains marks show start and end of speech

misconceptions.coach: Only the spoken words go in quotation marks, not 'Mum said'.
Speech needs quotation marks around the spoken words.

practiceItems.prompt: quotation marks go around the ___ words
the punctuation that introduces a list
the mark that separates items in a list
do quotation marks go around what a person says? (yes/no)

blocks.content: When you write a person's exact words, quotation marks go around them: Maya said, "I am ready." Notice the comma before the speech and the end mark inside the quotes. Let's practise the commas!
